meaning: Line 516 shapes the second manoeuvre transition with a quintic smoothstep (6x^5-15x^4+10x^3) of the clamped ramp fraction, so the driven quantity starts and ends with zero slope. It sets how abruptly the second onset is applied over `duration`.

could_move.what: Second-onset transient shape in the jugular compression comparison against patient data; a different smoothing changes peak rate of change and the fitted response.
The same smoothstep is repeated for transitions 1 and 3, so the profile must stay consistent across all three onsets in this element.
Stiff-solver step behaviour: a less smooth onset can change the dtmax needed near the transition.
h-parameter sweeps built on these drivers could shift, since sweep outputs depend on onset shape.
The parallel copies in Model_1 and Model_3 would diverge if only the celia copy is edited.

expectation: Unknown in size. Direction: a smoother (higher-order) transition lowers the peak time derivative at onset and delays the effective mid-point; a sharper one raises it. The plateau after `duration` is probably unchanged, but I cannot confirm that from the lines shown.

check.why: Runs the single case that uses this element so you can inspect the second onset transient without a re-fit.
